interests.title: AI for Software Engineering
interests.description: Investigating how large language models and AI agents can augment, automate, and transform software engineering practices. This includes automated code documentation, intelligent code generation, AI-assisted debugging, and the broader question of how AI changes the way software is designed, built, and maintained. My work on an LLM-powered code documentation system and context-aware AI development workflows at Therap has demonstrated both the potential and the open challenges in this space.

interests.title: Reliable and Trustworthy AI Agents
interests.description: Exploring the reliability, safety, and correctness guarantees needed when AI agents operate as autonomous components within production software systems. My experience building a multi-tenant AI Data Assistant that generates SQL queries from natural language has highlighted critical challenges around hallucination prevention, output verification, security enforcement, and graceful failure handling in agentic systems.

interests.title: Natural Language Interfaces for Data Systems
interests.description: Researching the design and safety challenges of enabling natural-language access to structured data systems. My work building a zero-data-leakage multi-tenant NL-to-SQL layer over millions of healthcare claims has surfaced critical open questions around semantic parsing accuracy, security guarantees, user intent disambiguation, and the gap between research benchmarks and production requirements.

interests.title: Context Engineering for LLM-based Systems
interests.description: Studying how structured context management, retrieval-augmented generation, and memory architectures can improve the reliability and effectiveness of LLM-powered tools. I designed and deployed MCP-connected context-aware workflows that reduced development time by 40% on a large-scale legacy codebase, demonstrating the practical impact of well-engineered context pipelines on AI agent performance.
